# 1 Maccabees Chapter 13 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, 1 Maccabees 13 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/1MA_013_page_001.jpg

---

**1** When Simon got word that Trypho was massing a huge army to invade and destroy Judea,

**2** he could see that the people were paralyzed with fear. He went up to Jerusalem and called a public assembly.

**3** He stood before them and said: "You know what my family has given — my father, my brothers, myself — for the sake of the law and the sanctuary. You have seen the wars, the suffering, everything we went through.

**4** All my brothers gave their lives for Israel's sake. I alone am left.

**5** And I will not spare my own life when my people are in danger. I am no better than my brothers.

**6** I will fight for my nation, for the sanctuary, for your wives and children. Every nation around us wants us gone — they hate us and want to destroy us."

**7** Those words put fire back into the people.

**8** They shouted back: "You are our leader — you stand in the place of Judas and Jonathan.

**9** Lead us into battle. Whatever you say, we will do."

**10** He immediately set the fighting men to work completing the fortification of Jerusalem.

**11** He sent Jonathan son of Absalom with a strong force to Joppa; Jonathan threw out the inhabitants and held the city.

**12** Trypho came up from the south with a large army and encamped at Adora. Simon matched him move for move.

**13** Trypho maneuvered to Baskama and encamped there.

**14** Trypho then realized he was not going to get at Jonathan while Simon was watching him. He sent a message to Simon:

**15** "Your brother owes the royal treasury one hundred talents of silver from the offices he held. He also left two sons as hostages with us. Pay the money and hand over the boys, and we'll let him go.

**16** Otherwise, no deal."

**17** Simon knew perfectly well it was a lie. But he sent the money and the boys anyway — because if Jonathan died and he hadn't sent them, people would blame him.

**18** They'd say: "Simon let his brother die to save a hundred talents."

**19** He sent both. Trypho took them and freed no one.

**20** Trypho moved on anyway, taking the road through Adora, heading into Judea to ravage it. Simon stayed on him, tracking every turn.

**21** The garrison in the Jerusalem citadel sent a secret message to Trypho: come through the wilderness and bring us supplies.

**22** Trypho got his cavalry ready to march that night — but a massive snowstorm shut everything down. He couldn't move. He pulled back and headed into Gilead instead.

**23** Near Baskama, he had Jonathan killed. Jonathan was buried there.

**24** Trypho turned around and went home.

**25** Simon sent for his brother Jonathan's bones and brought them to Modein, the family's hometown, for burial.

**26** All Israel mourned deeply for Jonathan for many days.

**27** Simon then built a splendid monument over the family tomb — his father's and his brothers' — faced with polished stone, rising high enough to be seen from a distance.

**28** He erected seven pyramids in a row, one for each: his father, his mother, his four brothers.

**29** He topped the monument with great columns, and on the columns hung suits of armor — a permanent memorial. Beside the armor, he had ships carved in relief, so that the tomb could be seen by sailors passing at sea.

**30** This is the tomb at Modein. It was still standing when this book was written.

**31** Trypho then dealt treacherously with young King Antiochus and murdered him.

**32** He seized the throne, crowned himself king of Asia, and his reign brought ruin on the land.

**33** Simon set to work fortifying Judea — high towers, massive walls, barred gates on every stronghold, with stockpiles of food inside.

**34** He also sent an embassy to Demetrius asking him to lift all the burdens from the land, since Trypho's only activity was looting it.

**35** Demetrius replied:

**36** "King Demetrius to Simon the high priest and Friend of Kings, and to the elders and to the people of the Jews, greetings.

**37** The golden wreath and the palm branch you sent us — received and accepted. We are ready to conclude a comprehensive peace with you and to write to the royal officials to grant you all exemptions.

**38** Whatever we have previously confirmed to you stands. The strongholds you have built are yours.

**39** We forgive all violations and infractions up to this date. The crown tax you owe is cancelled. Whatever levies were formerly collected in Jerusalem — they're done, finished.

**40** Any of you who qualify to serve in our army, enroll. And let there be peace between us."

**41** In the year 142 BCE, the yoke of the Gentiles was lifted from Israel.

**42** The people began dating their documents: "In the first year of Simon, great high priest, commander, and leader of the Jews."

**43** Simon moved against Gazara and besieged it with a full siege operation. He brought up a siege tower, rolled it against the walls, breached a tower, and took it.

**44** The men in the siege engine jumped down into the city. Chaos broke out inside.

**45** The people of Gazara poured up onto the wall — men, women, children — tearing their clothes, screaming at the tops of their voices, begging Simon to show mercy;

**46** "Don't treat us the way we deserve — treat us with kindness."

**47** Simon relented and stopped the assault. He expelled the population and purified every building that had housed idols. He entered the city to the sound of psalms and blessings.

**48** He removed every trace of impurity, resettled it with people who kept the law, reinforced the fortifications, and moved in himself.

**49** The Jerusalem citadel garrison was sealed off — no access to the country, no buying or selling. Supplies ran out. Men began to starve. Many died.

**50** The garrison sent out cries for mercy and surrender. Simon accepted. He expelled them and had the citadel purified from its defilements.

**51** It was the twenty-third day of the second month, 141 BCE, when Simon entered the citadel — amid songs of praise, waving palm branches, to music of harps, cymbals, and lutes, with hymns and psalms, because a great enemy had been crushed and driven out of Israel.

**52** He declared it an annual feast day, to be celebrated with joy and gladness every year. He strengthened the temple mount adjacent to the citadel and made it his own residence.

**53** When Simon saw that his son John had grown into a man, he appointed him commander-in-chief of all the forces and sent him to live at Gazara.
